notes: Large brown wooden park-rules board at Tikal; only the header lines are transcribed. Below are 16 Maya-glyph-framed prohibition pictograms with bilingual captions (NO ARMAS / NO GUNS, NO VEHICULOS / NO VEHICLES, ... NO BEBIDAS ALCOHOLICAS / NO ALCOHOL), which are distractors for the place query. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

author: Simon Burchell
attribution: Photo: Simon Burchell, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:El_Chal_1.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Hand-painted IDAEH board on two wooden posts at the entrance of El Chal archaeological site (Petén), with a smaller brown arrow sign 'Sitio Arqueológico El Chal' at right. Main board has no accents.

author: Guatemalancandies
attribution: Photo: Guatemalancandies, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:OFICINAS_CENTRALES.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Round logo sign with a smiling bear on the gable of the Guandy confectionery factory/offices, Guatemala City. A small green street sign on the pole at right reads 'A PERIFERICO NORTE' (with up arrow); two 'NO ESTACIONAR' signs on the wall are distractors.
source_categories: Photographs of road signs in Spanish language

author: Infrogmation of New Orleans
attribution: Photo: Infrogmation of New Orleans, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:S_Agustin_church,_Antigua_Guatemala,_1981_Sign.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Scroll-shaped bilingual plaque in blackletter-style script on the ruined San Agustín church, Antigua Guatemala; faded 1981 colour print. 'Innugurada' is spelled with a double n on the plaque; no accent on Agustin.
source_title: File:S Agustin church, Antigua Guatemala, 1981 Sign.jpg

author: Андрей Бобровский
attribution: Photo: Андрей Бобровский, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Tikal,_Guatemala_-_panoramio_(30).jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Overhanging distributor sign with globe logo and parrot mascot in Santa Elena (Petén); a second identical sign further right. Wires cross the sign. Distractors: 'Amilcar's Super Repuestos' / '...lcar's Super Auto Repuestos', 'Ursa', 'Qualimax', 'FARMACIA', 'CLINICAS MEDICAS', 'Way' signs; tuk-tuk '703' in foreground. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

author: Simon Burchell
attribution: Photo: Simon Burchell, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Zaculeu_01.JPG. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Spanish/Mam welcome billboard at the Zaculeu archaeological park, Huehuetenango ('B'A'N KYULENA' and 'Kyja qchman' are Mam; the apostrophes are typographic ’ on the sign). Footer logos: Gobierno de Guatemala, Ministerio de Cultura y Deportes, IDAEH. A smaller info board 'Centro arqueológico Zaculeu' below right has unreadable small text. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

author: Adam Jones from Kelowna, BC, Canada
attribution: Photo: Adam Jones from Kelowna, BC, Canada, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Detail_of_Sign_at_Entrance_to_Site_-_K%27umarcaaj_(Former_K%27iche%27_Capital)_-_Outside_Santa_Cruz_del_Quiche_-_Quiche_-_Guatemala_(15916576856).jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Rusty IDAEH site sign at Q'umarkaj near Santa Cruz del Quiché, covered in scratched graffiti (names ARACELY, KEVIN, BYRON...). Top line is cut off at the frame edge; 'DEPARTAMENTO DE MONUMENTOS' is heavily rusted; decree numbers after 'DECRETOS' are scratched out (looks like '425 Y 26-97', not certain). Black arrow pointing right. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.

author: Flickr user: David Dennis
attribution: Photo: Flickr user: David Dennis, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Una_Via.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Yellow colonial tile street plaque in Antigua Guatemala with a Dominican coat of arms (two dogs with torches) between the words: read 'CALLE DE' across the top and 'STO. DOMINGO' across the bottom. Black-and-white 'UNA VIA' one-way tile sign with arrow below.

author: Infrogmation of New Orleans
attribution: Photo: Infrogmation of New Orleans, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:GuateCityElCairo.jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Faded 1979 colour print of Sexta Avenida, zona 1, Guatemala City: red rooftop letters 'EL CAIRO' over the department store at right (preceded by a small illegible word), and 'EL CAIRO' again on the facade. Distractors: an 'ALMACEN EL CAIRO' panel down the street, 'HOTEL', many unreadable signs, street clock; cars with small plates.

author: seth pipkin

notes: Crush-sponsored shop sign over a corner store in Cobán on a rainy, flooded street; big painted 'TIENDA' and 'Se Alquila Telefono' on the building below. Distractors: 'IMPRENTA / MEDI...
